evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v. Parisii: Parisii, Lutetia, Loticia Parisiorum, Parisius, Parisis, Paris
terms.comment: Named after the Parīsiī, the people whose town it was; Morgan–Owens finds it much more common in printed books. A town takes no preposition: Parīsiōs (to), Parīsiīs (in, at), Parīsiīs (from).
The ancient name, in full Lutetia Parīsiōrum (Caes. BG 6.3); in later Latin it belongs to the high style (M-O, citing Vives).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus, edition of F. Benedict (1909), Latin–German, read in the digitization at columbia.edu (cited as Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v.); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
